Really good first commit. A few things to consider modifying.
If you are trying to defer emitting signals until the interface is all set up, then you probably want to pass the second parameter skipSignal=true?
Done

Generally, I think it is good to let an object "handle its own business". Provide a layer of abstraction so that if the internals change, users of the object don't have to make code updates.

It seems like lines 36-57 could be within a Chassis::initializePowerSystemInputStatus() method instead? The System class probably doesn't need to know about these internal details of the Chassis class. Let the Chassis class define its own object path, create the ChassisPowerSystemInterface that it will own, handle the exception, etc.
Done

We are encouraged to minimize the amount of informational journal messages we write. The journal space is limited, and it wraps when it gets full.

So the journal should contain only high importance info messages along with key error messages.

This message should probably be removed. I'll leave it up to you whether you consider the one on line 30 to be highly important.

Another option is to use lg2::debug(). These are discarded by default, but you can modify a journal setting during testing to log the debug messages. I've used this before. The only trick is that other apps have debug messages too, so the journal can get pretty noisy.
Done

Why is this deleted? The data type still appears on line 68.

The best practice is to have each file explicitly #include any data types/constants that is uses. It should not rely on getting the include "second hand" from some other include (such as chassis.hpp).

The only deviation is that source files don't need to re-include things that their header file includes. So system.cpp doesn't need to include something if system.hpp already does. The two are kind of one file split into two pieces due to the way the C++ compiler/linker work.
I had removed it as chassis included it. I will add it back.
Could just directly assign return value from std::make_unique() to the data member and skip the local var interface right?
Done
Doxygen comment has wrong description/parameter.
Done

Thank you for moving this functionality into the Chassis class.

I think it would make more sense to call this method initializePowerSystemInputsInterface() or something similar now.

Usually with a setX() method, it is setting the X data member to the passed in parameter value. That is no longer true here. We are asking the object to initialize/create this itself.
Done
Done

Would it make sense to change this to initializePowerSystemInputs?

From the name, it sounds like it might just be setting the Status property on an interface that already exists. But it is actually creating the interface.

That would also be consistent with the Chassis method name if you rename that one.

Big picture, I would recommend the following pattern where it makes sense: System::foo() loops over all the Chassis objects and calls Chassis::foo() on each one.

If System is going to delegate something to the Chassis (which it often should), then it is easer to understand if the Chassis method has the same name.
